title: C4368A — Body Control Module B connector guide
introduction:
I read this connector reference as the body controller’s electrical address book. Its tables connect cavity labels with power supplies, ground, lighting functions, window commands and network communication. That helps explain why this plug carries several kinds of electrical business under the same roof.

Start with the connector identity table, then match a cavity label in the drawing to the Cavity column in the assignment table. Read across the entire row: Circuit Number identifies the circuit, Color records its wire-color code, Function describes its role, and Terminal Part Number identifies the listed terminal. Keep repeated cavity rows separate; their blank Qualifier cells do not explain which listing applies. The protection descriptions retain a fuse-or-circuit-breaker alternative.

The drawing has centered end cavities and paired columns between them. Gray-filled positions correspond to blank circuit and function entries in the table. Housing projections help distinguish the pictured shape, but their release or locking functions are not labeled. The summary pin count conflicts with the illustrated cavity range and needs clarification.

This guide supports reading the reference. Physical viewing direction, access, electrical tests and replacement instructions are outside its scope. Gauge, Size and Used entries remain as printed; no gauge convention or code legend is supplied, so they are not a basis for choosing wire or test equipment.

edits.why: I use the centered end cavities and the housing’s asymmetric side projections as landmarks within this drawing. Matching the printed cavity labels to the table avoids relying on apparent left and right, especially because the physical viewing side is unspecified.

The table separates supply and ground connections from lighting, window-control and network functions. A function label identifies a circuit’s job; it does not establish a test result or condemn the controller. Repeated listings remain separate because their applicability is unexplained.

A pigtail is a connector with attached wire leads. The service-parts section supports identifying listed repair components; a kit listing alone does not establish compatibility or teach terminal removal, splicing or installation.

originalAuthorHold: The identity table states Pin Count 34, while the supplied face drawing labels cavities 1–24 and the assignment table uses that same cavity range. The evidence does not resolve what the stated pin count represents; retain the original data pending review.

editorialRevision.scope: Complete independent active-agent review of all 63 primary units including complete pigtail table u60–u62 and raw-text u63 omitted from original 59-unit first CLI chunk coverage, four complete source pages and sole figure, and 3 edits. All public fields unchanged from original author. Count and repeated lighting/network assignments remain unresolved for bounded reference reading only.
